title: Chapter VI — The Founder and Faculty of Savoy College
text:
Chapter VI

The Founder and Faculty of Savoy College

If this history of Savoy Male and Female College is to be regarded as an examination of a forward step in the program of education in Texas, something more must be given than the external facts of school plant, enrollment, and the human interest of campus life, for obviously the development of such a college was an expression of the character of a wide-reaching neighborhood of people of advanced ideals, and its success was rooted in the support of the community's leading citizens. There is additional significance, therefore, in the personnel of the founders and the faculty which was drawn to the work under the leadership of President Halsell. For a more adequate understanding of the significance of the College, therefore, this biographical chapter includes sketches of three trustees, as representative of the citizenship of the section, in addition to biographies of the three principals who are the central figures in the story of Savoy Male and Female College.

J. L. German, Thomas J. Chenoweth, and James Paxton married sisters of Miss Eliza German and Mr. Paxton had married sister of Mr. Chenoweth. Within a short time they had begun to prosper as farmers in the region, with their own and their neighbors' families coming on, they were ready to give support to the College. President Halsell had already begun to teach in the section, and with him they were ready to support the cause of education. With President Halsell had already begun to teach in the section, and with him they and with a German, President Holland and Halsell as instructors, were ready to give support to the College. All three were members of the Christian Church. This homogeneity of ideals and attitudes was an important element in the success of Savoy College.
